newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Cosatu to go ahead with June 2 strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Cosatu to go ahead with June 2 strike.

text.p: The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) on Tuesday confirmed plans for a national strike on June 2 and said it would appeal against a labour court ruling that had forced it to postpone the action.
The 1.9 million strong labour federation said in a statement the leadership call for a 24-hour strike was endorsed by the executive committee on Monday.
"The form of action will be a 24-hour strike. This is because of the widening gap in the negotiations as well as their (business and government) hardening of attitudes," the federation said.
The statement said Cosatu would strike against aspects of the draft Basic Conditions of Employment Act, which sets minimum employment standards for the first time.
Cosatu wants the working week reduced from the proposed 45-hour ceiling to 40 hours, four months of paid maternity leave and the minimum age for formal employment to be set at 18.
The union federation rejected last week's decision by a three-member labour court panel to outlaw a proposed half-day strike on May 12.
It said lawyers had been instructed to appeal to the Constitutional Court against the decision.
